subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Variety of living organisms: plants and animals
Variety of living organisms: fungi, bacteria and protoctists

questions.q: Which term describes the removal of the waste products of metabolic reactions from the body?
questions.explain: Excretion is the removal of the waste products of metabolism, such as carbon dioxide and urea.

questions.q: The characteristics of living organisms can be summarised by MRS GREN. What does the 'N' stand for?
questions.explain: In MRS GREN the 'N' stands for nutrition, the taking in of materials for energy, growth and development.

questions.q: A plant shoot growing towards a source of light is an example of which characteristic of living organisms?
questions.explain: Sensitivity is the ability to detect and respond to changes in the surroundings, such as the direction of light.

questions.q: Which characteristic must all living organisms carry out in order to release energy from their food?
questions.explain: Respiration releases energy from food molecules and is carried out by all living organisms.

questions.q: What substance makes up the cell walls of plants?
questions.explain: Plant cells have cell walls made of cellulose, which provides support.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a flowering plant that is a cereal?
questions.explain: Maize is a cereal, whereas the pea is a herbaceous legume.

questions.q: Why are animals unable to make their own food by photosynthesis?
options: Their cells have cellulose cell walls
questions.explain: Animal cells contain no chloroplasts, so they cannot photosynthesise and must obtain food from other organisms.

questions.q: An organism is multicellular, has no cell walls, coordinates its actions using a nervous system and stores carbohydrate as glycogen. To which group does it belong?
questions.explain: The absence of cell walls, nervous coordination and glycogen storage are all typical features of animals.

questions.q: The cell walls of fungi are made of which substance?
questions.explain: Fungal cell walls are made of chitin, not the cellulose found in plant cell walls.

questions.q: Fungi feed by secreting digestive enzymes onto their food and then absorbing the dissolved products. What is this type of nutrition called?
questions.explain: Saprotrophic nutrition involves extracellular digestion, where enzymes are secreted onto food and the products are absorbed.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes yeast?
options: It is a multicellular fungus made of hyphae
questions.explain: Yeast is a single-celled fungus, unlike Mucor whose body is organised into a mycelium of hyphae.

questions.q: Which of these structures is NOT found in a bacterial cell?
questions.explain: Bacteria have no nucleus; their genetic material is a circular chromosome of DNA together with plasmids.

questions.q: Lactobacillus bulgaricus is a rod-shaped bacterium. In which process is it used?
questions.explain: Lactobacillus bulgaricus is used to make yoghurt from milk.

questions.q: Chlorella is a protoctist whose cells contain chloroplasts. This means that Chlorella can...
questions.explain: Chlorella has chloroplasts, so like plant cells it can photosynthesise.

questions.q: Which protoctist causes the disease malaria?
questions.explain: Plasmodium is a pathogenic protoctist that causes malaria.

questions.q: A microscopic single-celled organism has a cell wall, cytoplasm, plasmids and a circular loop of DNA, but no nucleus. What is it?
questions.explain: The lack of a nucleus together with plasmids and a circular DNA chromosome are defining features of bacteria.

questions.q: An organism is made of thread-like hyphae forming a mycelium, has cell walls containing chitin and cannot photosynthesise. To which group does it belong?
questions.explain: Hyphae forming a mycelium and chitin cell walls are characteristic features of fungi.

questions.q: Pneumococcus is described as a pathogen. What does this mean?
options: It is used to make yoghurt
It lives only in pond water
questions.explain: A pathogen is a disease-causing organism; Pneumococcus is a spherical bacterium that causes pneumonia.

questions.q: Which statement about viruses is correct?
options: They contain one type of nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) surrounded by a protein coat
They have a nucleus containing DNA
They have cell walls made of chitin
questions.explain: Viruses have no cellular structure; they consist of a protein coat surrounding one type of nucleic acid, either DNA or RNA.

questions.q: A particle is smaller than a bacterium, has no cytoplasm or cell membrane, consists of a protein coat surrounding RNA, and can reproduce only inside living cells. What is it?
questions.explain: Only viruses lack cellular structure, have a protein coat around nucleic acid, and can reproduce solely inside living host cells.
